assets.alpha_note: Saved RGBA composited on dark and pale backgrounds has no visible halo, haze or ground patch. This is a visual-alpha verdict, not a claim that every off-subject alpha sample is exactly zero.
differences: Try3 replaces the previously rejected nearly continuous wavy timber grooves with separated thin longitudinal marks and quiet intervening planes.
Timber pigment is less pale and more irregularly shaded, with a restrained darker lower/right tone closer to the adopted bench and waterwheel.
The stone basin and counterweight remain somewhat more mottled than the timber; this stays subordinate at game scale.
Outer edges remain more continuous than some locked bark fragments, but are sufficiently fine and variable to avoid the previous smooth outlined-icon treatment.
assets.reasoning: Direct raw and 1x/2x comparison with rejected working2 shows a material correction, not only a semantic or numeric pass. The principal wood surfaces now contain sparse interrupted grain marks, restrained pigment variation and quiet broad areas; the repeated long grooves and polished pale strip appearance no longer dominate. At production size the warmer, darker timber sits consistently beside the woodworking bench and waterwheel. The left pivot, supported lever, compression post contacting the platen, guide and suspended counterweight retain a coherent press mechanism. Olive material, outlet stream and receiving jar retain the working-state cue. Upper-left light and visually clean saved RGBA agree with the family. This pass applies only to working try3; empty try3 remains a capped style rejection.
